# Exploratory data analysis

## variables asked only in 2025, 2024, 2022, 2019, and 2017

`NOBCUSE9` = What was main reason for not doing anything to keep you from getting pregnant? `PFPPRVN4` = The last time you had sexual intercourse, did you or your partner do anything to keep you from getting pregnant? () `FAMILY PLANNING` = The last time you had sexual intercourse, what did you or your partner do to keep you from getting pregnant? (lots of response categories!!!)

## variables asked in all surveys

`SEXVAR` = 2 if female

`MARITAL`= marital status (1=married, 2=divorced, 3=widowed, 4=separated, 5=never married,6=A member of an unmarried couple, 9 =refused)

`HOME`= homeowner status (1=own, 2=rent, 3=other arrangement, 7=don't know, 9=refused)

`PREGNANT` = current pregnancy status (1=yes, 2=no, 7=don't know, 9=refused)

`MENTHLTH` = Now thinking about your mental health, which includes stress, depression, and problems with emotions, for how many days during the past 30 days was your mental health not good? (1-30, 88=none,77=don't know, 99=refused)

`EMPLOY` = employment status (1 = employed for wages, 2 = self-employed, 3 = out of work for 1 year or more, 4 = out of work for less than 1 year, 5 = homemaker, 6 = student, 7 = retired, 8 = unable to work, 9 = refused)

`INCOME` = income categories (1=less than 15k, 2=15k to 25k, 3= 25k to 35k, 4= 35k to 50k, 5=50k to 100k, 6=100k to 200k, 7=200k or more, 9=don't know)

`EDUCA` = What is the highest grade or year of school you completed? (1=no high school, 2=high school, 3=some college,4=college,9=don't know)

`INSURANCE` = Respondents aged 18-64 who have any form of health insurance (1=yes, 2=no, 9=don't know)

`RACE` = Race/ethnicity categories (1=nh white, 2=nh black, 3=nh native american, 4=nh asian, 5=nh native hawaiian, 7=nh multiracial,9=don't know)

## subset each survey year to include relevant variables, subsetting the sample to only women

## merge relevant questionnaire years

```{r}
data_list <- list(
  `2017` = sub_dat17,
  `2019` = sub_dat19,
  `2022` = sub_dat22,
  `2024` = sub_dat24,
  `2025` = sub_dat25
)

vars_to_keep <- c(
  "_STATE",
  "_AGEG5YR",
  "PREGNANT",
  "MENTHLTH",
  "EMPLOY",
  "INCOME",
  "EDUCA",
  "INSURANCE",
  "RACE",
  "MARITAL",
  "HOME",
  "FAMILY_PLANNING",
  "IYEAR",
  "IMONTH",
  "IDAY"
)

analysis_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  data_list,
  function(dataset, year) {

    year <- as.integer(year)

    dataset <- dataset |>
      dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(vars_to_keep)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        YEAR = year
      )

    if (year == 2022) {
      dataset <- dataset |>
        dplyr::mutate(
          IYEAR = as.integer(as.character(IYEAR)),
          IMONTH = as.integer(as.character(IMONTH)),
          IDAY = as.integer(as.character(IDAY)),

          date = as.Date(
            sprintf("%04d-%02d-%02d", IYEAR, IMONTH, IDAY)
          ),

          post_ban = dplyr::case_when(
            date < as.Date("2022-06-24") ~ 0L,
            date >= as.Date("2022-06-24") ~ 1L,
            TRUE ~ NA_integer_
          )
        )
    } else {
      dataset <- dataset |>
        dplyr::mutate(
          date = as.Date(NA),

          POST_BAN = dplyr::case_when(
            YEAR <= 2021 ~ 0L,
            YEAR >= 2023 ~ 1L,
            TRUE ~ NA_integer_
          )
        )
    }

    dataset
  }
) |>
  dplyr::rename(STATE = `_STATE`) |> select(-c(IYEAR, IMONTH, IDAY, date))


# check that post ban was correctly created
analysis_data |> filter(YEAR == 2025) |> janitor::tabyl(post_ban)
analysis_data |> filter(YEAR == 2024) |> janitor::tabyl(post_ban)
analysis_data |> filter(YEAR == 2022) |> janitor::tabyl(post_ban)
analysis_data |> filter(YEAR == 2019) |> janitor::tabyl(post_ban)
analysis_data |> filter(YEAR == 2017) |> janitor::tabyl(post_ban)
```

```{r}
  dplyr::left_join(
    census_region_lookup,
    by = "STATE"
  ) |> filter(!is.na(REGION)) |> rename(AGEG5YR = "_AGEG5YR")
```

```{r}
get_descriptive_stats_over_entire_period <- function(data, var) {
  
  tab <- data |>
    janitor::tabyl(
      {{ var }},
      show_na = TRUE
    )
  
  # The first column is the categorical variable
  category_col <- names(tab)[1]
  
  total_n <- sum(tab$n)
  
  valid_n <- sum(
    tab$n[!is.na(tab[[category_col]])]
  )
  
  tab |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      percent = 100 * n / total_n,
      valid_percent = dplyr::if_else(
        valid_n > 0 & !is.na(.data[[category_col]]),
        100 * n / valid_n,
        NA_real_
      )
    )
}
```

## Trends in the U.S. Regions Over Time

```{r}
regional_summary <- analysis_data_v2 |>
  select(
    STATE,
    REGION,
    YEAR,
    all_of(variables_to_summarize)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(variables_to_summarize),
    names_to = "VARIABLE",
    values_to = "VALUE"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    VALUE_CODE = if_else(
      is.na(VALUE),
      "Missing",
      as.character(VALUE)
    ),

    VALUE_LABEL = map2_chr(
      VARIABLE,
      VALUE_CODE,
      function(variable, code) {
        if (code == "Missing") {
          return("Missing")
        }

        label <- unname(variable_labels[[variable]][code])

        if (is.na(label)) {
          paste("Unlabeled code:", code)
        } else {
          label
        }
      }
    )
  ) |>
  count(
    STATE,
    REGION,
    YEAR,
    VARIABLE,
    VALUE_CODE,
    VALUE_LABEL,
    name = "N"
  ) |>
  group_by(STATE, REGION, YEAR, VARIABLE) |>
  mutate(
    PERCENT = round(100 * N / sum(N),2)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
}
```

## Nonresponse and special response codes

Blank values and explicit don't-know/refused codes are reported separately. Pregnancy comparisons are restricted to ages 18–49 because older respondents were not asked this item. These are unweighted, pooled descriptive rates; they are not population estimates.

```{r}
nonresponse_codes <- list(
  PREGNANT = c(7, 9), MENTHLTH = c(77, 99), EMPLOY = c(9),
  INCOME = c(9), EDUCA = c(9), INSURANCE = c(9),
  RACE = c(9), MARITAL = c(9), HOME = c(7, 9)
)

age_eligible_data <- analysis_data_v2 |> filter(AGEG5YR %in% 1:6)

missingness_summary_18_49 <- purrr::imap_dfr(nonresponse_codes, function(codes, variable) {
  x <- age_eligible_data[[variable]]
  blank_n <- sum(is.na(x))
  special_n <- sum(!is.na(x) & x %in% codes)
  tibble(
    VARIABLE = variable,
    BLANK_N = blank_n,
    UNKNOWN_OR_REFUSED_N = special_n,
    TOTAL_UNREPORTED_N = blank_n + special_n,
    PERCENT_UNREPORTED = round(100 * (blank_n + special_n) / length(x), 1)
  )
}) |> arrange(desc(PERCENT_UNREPORTED))

knitr::kable(missingness_summary_18_49,
             caption = "Blank plus explicit unknown/refused codes, ages 18–49")
```

## Family planning responses and missingness (2025)

The 2025 family-planning module is summarized separately because its questions and response categories do not line up exactly with the earlier survey waves. These summaries use women respondents in the 2025 file. Blank responses include structural skips and states that may not have included this module, so the tables distinguish full-sample blanks from blanks among age-eligible respondents in states with recorded module responses. The respondent eligibility follows questionnaire routing: ages 18–49 and not coded as currently pregnant, then the preceding answer where applicable. Counts and percentages below are unweighted.

```{r}
family_planning_data <- sub_dat25 |>
  mutate(
    age_18_49 = `_AGEG5YR` %in% 1:6,
    not_coded_currently_pregnant = is.na(PREGNANT) | as.numeric(PREGNANT) != 1,
    module_eligible = age_18_49 & not_coded_currently_pregnant
  )

family_planning_labels <- list(
  HADSEX = c(
    `1` = "Yes", `2` = "No", `7` = "Don't know/not sure", `9` = "Refused"
  ),
  PREVENT_PREGNANCY = c(
    `1` = "Yes", `2` = "No", `7` = "Don't know/not sure", `9` = "Refused"
  ),
  FAMILY_PLANNING = c(
    `1` = "Female sterilization", `2` = "Male sterilization",
    `3` = "Implant", `4` = "IUD", `5` = "Shots",
    `6` = "Prescription pills, ring, or patch", `7` = "Over-the-counter pill",
    `8` = "Condoms", `9` = "Diaphragm, gel, cap, or similar",
    `10` = "Fertility awareness/rhythm", `11` = "Withdrawal",
    `12` = "Emergency contraception", `13` = "Other method",
    `77` = "Don't know/not sure", `99` = "Refused"
  ),
  NO_PREVENT_REASON = c(
    `1` = "No expected sex/no regular partner", `2` = "Did not think about it",
    `3` = "Wanted a pregnancy", `4` = "Did not care if pregnant",
    `5` = "Did not want to use birth control", `6` = "Trouble getting/paying for birth control",
    `8` = "Thought pregnancy was not possible", `9` = "Using withdrawal",
    `10` = "Female sterilization", `11` = "Partner vasectomy",
    `12` = "Breastfeeding/recent birth", `14` = "Other reason",
    `77` = "Don't know/not sure", `99` = "Refused"
  )
)

family_planning_distribution <- purrr::imap_dfr(family_planning_labels, function(labels, variable) {
  raw <- as.numeric(family_planning_data[[variable]])
  observed_codes <- ifelse(is.na(raw), "BLANK", as.character(raw))
  counts <- tibble(RESPONSE_CODE = observed_codes) |>
    count(RESPONSE_CODE, name = "N")
  response_levels <- c(names(labels), "BLANK")
  tibble(
    VARIABLE = variable,
    RESPONSE_CODE = response_levels,
    RESPONSE = c(unname(labels), "Not asked or blank")
  ) |>
    left_join(counts, by = "RESPONSE_CODE") |>
    mutate(
      N = tidyr::replace_na(N, 0L),
      PERCENT_OF_ALL_2025_WOMEN = round(100 * N / nrow(family_planning_data), 2),
      PERCENT_OF_NONBLANK_RESPONSES = if_else(
        RESPONSE_CODE == "BLANK", NA_real_,
        round(100 * N / sum(N[RESPONSE_CODE != "BLANK"]), 2)
      )
    )
})

knitr::kable(family_planning_distribution,
             caption = "Family-planning response counts and unweighted percentages, 2025 women respondents")

state_module_coverage <- family_planning_data |>
  filter(module_eligible, !is.na(`_STATE`)) |>
  group_by(`_STATE`) |>
  summarise(
    AGE_ELIGIBLE_N = n(),
    HADSEX_RECORDED_N = sum(!is.na(HADSEX)),
    HADSEX_RECORDED_PERCENT = round(100 * HADSEX_RECORDED_N / AGE_ELIGIBLE_N, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(HADSEX_RECORDED_PERCENT)

knitr::kable(state_module_coverage,
             caption = "State-level recorded response coverage for HADSEX among age/pregnancy-eligible women")

ggplot(state_module_coverage,
       aes(x = reorder(`_STATE`, HADSEX_RECORDED_PERCENT), y = HADSEX_RECORDED_PERCENT)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Recorded HADSEX responses vary across states",
       subtitle = "Share with a nonblank response among women ages 18–49 not coded currently pregnant",
       x = "State", y = "Percent with a recorded response") +
  theme_minimal()
```

States with no recorded responses may not have included the optional module. Confirm state-level questionnaire coverage before interpreting those blanks as individual nonresponse.

```{r}
states_with_family_planning_data <- state_module_coverage |>
  filter(HADSEX_RECORDED_N > 0) |>
  pull(`_STATE`)
family_planning_data$module_state_has_responses <- family_planning_data$`_STATE` %in% states_with_family_planning_data

question_eligibility <- list(
  HADSEX = family_planning_data$module_eligible & family_planning_data$module_state_has_responses,
  PREVENT_PREGNANCY = family_planning_data$module_eligible & family_planning_data$module_state_has_responses &
    !is.na(family_planning_data$HADSEX) & as.numeric(family_planning_data$HADSEX) == 1,
  FAMILY_PLANNING = family_planning_data$module_eligible & family_planning_data$module_state_has_responses &
    !is.na(family_planning_data$HADSEX) & as.numeric(family_planning_data$HADSEX) == 1 &
    !is.na(family_planning_data$PREVENT_PREGNANCY) & as.numeric(family_planning_data$PREVENT_PREGNANCY) == 1,
  NO_PREVENT_REASON = family_planning_data$module_eligible & family_planning_data$module_state_has_responses &
    !is.na(family_planning_data$HADSEX) & as.numeric(family_planning_data$HADSEX) == 1 &
    !is.na(family_planning_data$PREVENT_PREGNANCY) & as.numeric(family_planning_data$PREVENT_PREGNANCY) == 2
)

family_planning_missingness <- purrr::imap_dfr(question_eligibility, function(eligible, variable) {
  x <- as.numeric(family_planning_data[[variable]])
  special_codes <- if (variable %in% c("HADSEX", "PREVENT_PREGNANCY")) c(7, 9) else c(77, 99)
  tibble(
    VARIABLE = variable,
    FULL_SAMPLE_N = length(x),
    FULL_SAMPLE_BLANK_N = sum(is.na(x)),
    FULL_SAMPLE_BLANK_PERCENT = round(100 * mean(is.na(x)), 1),
    ELIGIBLE_IN_STATES_WITH_DATA_N = sum(eligible, na.rm = TRUE),
    ELIGIBLE_BLANK_N = sum(eligible & is.na(x), na.rm = TRUE),
    ELIGIBLE_BLANK_PERCENT = round(100 * sum(eligible & is.na(x), na.rm = TRUE) / max(1, sum(eligible, na.rm = TRUE)), 1),
    ELIGIBLE_DK_OR_REFUSED_N = sum(eligible & !is.na(x) & x %in% special_codes, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
})

knitr::kable(family_planning_missingness,
             caption = "Full-sample blanks versus blanks among eligible respondents in states with recorded family-planning responses")
```

# EDA: DATA COMPLETENESS AND MISSINGNESS BY YEAR
```{r}

# DATA COMPLETENESS AND MISSINGNESS BY YEAR

# Variables to assess
candidate_vars <- c(
  "PREGNANT",
  "MENTHLTH",
  "EMPLOY",
  "INCOME",
  "EDUCA",
  "INSURANCE",
  "RACE",
  "MARITAL",
  "HOME",
  "HADSEX","PFPPRVN4",
  "PREVENT_PREGNANCY",
  "FAMILY_PLANNING",
  "NOBCUSE9",
  "NO_PREVENT_REASON"
)

available_vars <- intersect(candidate_vars, names(analysis_data))

# Harmonize aliases to avoid double-counting the same question
if ("PREVENT_PREGNANCY" %in% available_vars &&
    "PFPPRVN4" %in% available_vars) {
  available_vars <- setdiff(available_vars, "PREVENT_PREGNANCY")
}

if ("NO_PREVENT_REASON" %in% available_vars &&
    "NOBCUSE9" %in% available_vars) {
  available_vars <- setdiff(available_vars, "NO_PREVENT_REASON")
}

if (length(available_vars) == 0) {
  stop("None of the requested variables are available.")
}
```

# Response Codes
```{r}

#  Special response codes: don't know/refused
special_codes <- list(
  PREGNANT = c(7, 9),
  MENTHLTH = c(77, 99),
  EMPLOY = c(9),
  INCOME = c(9),
  EDUCA = c(9),
  INSURANCE = c(9),
  RACE = c(9),
  MARITAL = c(9),
  HOME = c(7, 9),
  HADSEX = c(7, 9),
  PFPPRVN4 = c(7, 9),
  PREVENT_PREGNANCY = c(7, 9),
  FAMILY_PLANNING = c(77, 99),
  NOBCUSE9 = c(77, 99),
  NO_PREVENT_REASON = c(77, 99)
)


# 3. Make a long dataset without mixing variable storage types
completeness_long <- analysis_data_v2 |>
  mutate(
    AGE_ELIGIBLE = `_AGEG5YR` %in% 1:6
  ) |>
  select(YEAR, AGE_ELIGIBLE, all_of(available_vars)) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(available_vars), as.character)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(available_vars),
    names_to = "VARIABLE",
    values_to = "RESPONSE"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    RESPONSE = na_if(RESPONSE, ""),
    IS_BLANK = is.na(RESPONSE),
    IS_SPECIAL = map2_lgl(
      VARIABLE,
      RESPONSE,
      function(v, x) {
        codes <- special_codes[[v]]
        !is.na(x) && !is.null(codes) && x %in% as.character(codes)
      }
    )
  )

# 4. Overall completeness by year and variable
# Valid = nonblank and not explicitly don't know/refused.
# Blank values may include structural skips and unavailable modules.

completeness_by_year <- completeness_long |>
  group_by(YEAR, VARIABLE) |>
  summarise(
    TOTAL_N = n(),
    BLANK_N = sum(IS_BLANK),
    DK_REFUSED_N = sum(IS_SPECIAL),
    VALID_N = TOTAL_N - BLANK_N - DK_REFUSED_N,
    BLANK_PERCENT = round(100 * BLANK_N / TOTAL_N, 1),
    DK_REFUSED_PERCENT = round(100 * DK_REFUSED_N / TOTAL_N, 1),
    VALID_PERCENT = round(100 * VALID_N / TOTAL_N, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(VARIABLE, YEAR)

knitr::kable(
  completeness_by_year,
  caption = paste(
    "Completeness and nonresponse by survey year;",
    "unweighted pooled records"
  )
)

# 5. Graph: valid response percentage by year
ggplot(
  completeness_by_year,
  aes(
    x = YEAR,
    y = VALID_PERCENT,
    color = VARIABLE,
    group = VARIABLE
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Valid Response Completeness by Year",
    subtitle = "Blank and explicit unknown/refused responses excluded",
    x = "Survey year",
    y = "Valid responses (%)",
    color = "Variable"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# 6. Graph: blank percentage by year
ggplot(
  completeness_by_year,
  aes(
    x = YEAR,
    y = BLANK_PERCENT,
    color = VARIABLE,
    group = VARIABLE
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Blank Response Percentage by Year",
    subtitle = "Blanks can reflect skip logic or unavailable modules",
    x = "Survey year",
    y = "Blank responses (%)",
    color = "Variable"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")


```


# HeatMap for overall population

```{r}
# Valid % heatmap
ggplot(completeness_by_year,
       aes(x = factor(YEAR), y = fct_reorder(VARIABLE, VALID_PERCENT, .fun = mean),
           fill = VALID_PERCENT)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(VALID_PERCENT)), size = 3, color = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", limits = c(0, 100), na.value = "grey90") +
  labs(title = "Valid Response Completeness by Variable and Year",
       subtitle = "Blank and explicit DK/refused excluded",
       x = "Survey year", y = NULL, fill = "Valid %") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

```

# Stacked bar chart of response composition by variable and year
```{r}
completeness_by_year |>
  select(YEAR, VARIABLE, VALID_PERCENT, DK_REFUSED_PERCENT, BLANK_PERCENT) |>
  pivot_longer(ends_with("PERCENT"), names_to = "STATUS", values_to = "PCT") |>
  mutate(STATUS = factor(STATUS,
                         levels = c("BLANK_PERCENT","DK_REFUSED_PERCENT","VALID_PERCENT"),
                         labels = c("Blank / skipped","DK / refused","Valid"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(YEAR), PCT, fill = STATUS)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~ VARIABLE, ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Blank / skipped" = "grey80",
                               "DK / refused" = "orange",
                               "Valid" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(title = "Response Composition by Variable and Year",
       x = "Survey year", y = "% of records", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())


composition_table <- completeness_by_year |>
  select(YEAR, VARIABLE, VALID_PERCENT, DK_REFUSED_PERCENT, BLANK_PERCENT) |>
  rename(
    `Valid %`      = VALID_PERCENT,
    `DK/Refused %` = DK_REFUSED_PERCENT,
    `Blank/Skip %` = BLANK_PERCENT
  ) |>
  arrange(VARIABLE, YEAR)

knitr::kable(
  composition_table,
  caption = "Response composition (%) by variable and survey year",
  digits  = 1
)
```


# SANITY CHECK: AGE AND PREGNANCY total numbers

```{r}
analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(
    # _AGEG5YR: 1=18-24, 2=25-29, 3=30-34, 4=35-39, 5=40-44, 6=45-49,
    #           7=50-54, 8=55-59, ...
    AGE_18_49    = `_AGEG5YR` %in% 1:6,
    AGE_18_59    = `_AGEG5YR` %in% 1:8,
    NOT_PREGNANT = is.na(PREGNANT) | PREGNANT != 1
  )

# Now the sanity check works
analysis_data |>
  summarise(
    total_rows         = n(),
    women              = n(),
    age_18_49          = sum(AGE_18_49),
    age_18_49_not_preg = sum(AGE_18_49 & NOT_PREGNANT),
    preg_yes           = sum(PREGNANT == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    preg_dk_refused    = sum(PREGNANT %in% c(7, 9), na.rm = TRUE),
    preg_blank         = sum(is.na(PREGNANT))
  )
```
